subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose a plugin runtime caller for plugin-registered Gateway methods, and should that surface be raw method dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or a typed service/capability contract?
rationale: The implementation shape changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the method policy, caller attribution model, or API permanence.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep the route-scoped helper only
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and ask plugins to use existing HTTP route or capability seams instead.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method string caller and intentionally accept the larger security and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the nearest existing route-scoped dispatch contract and merged the admin HTTP RPC boundary that constrains this design.
